title: Normalized strict scalar unit for the regular completed coefficient complex
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $Y$. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $A_{F,m}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m$, $R_F=\varprojlim_{m\ge1}(A_{F,m})_Y$, and write $\pi^F_m:R_F\to(A_{F,m})_Y$ for the limit projections, for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the coefficient maps $\rho_m:R_E\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ induced by $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ as in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Let $P=R_E[0]$, and let $T_m=\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P\otimes_{R_E}(A_{L,m})_Y)$ with transition $t_m:T_{m+1}\to T_m$ induced by reduction. Tensors are sheafified tensors applied termwise [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; restriction uses $\pi^L_m$. Put $B=\prod_{m\ge1}T_m$ (termwise product) and $C_{E,L}=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)[-1]$, where $(1-s)(x)_m=x_m-t_m(x_{m+1})$, with the strict mapping-cocone convention and projections $\mathrm{fst}:C_{E,L}\to B$, $\mathrm{snd}:C_{E,L}\to B[-1]$ on graded objects. All complexes and derived categories are those of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

The complex $P$ is K-flat with flat terms over $R_E$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The multiplication maps
$$u_m:P\otimes_{R_E}(A_{L,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_{L,m})_Y[0],\qquad r\otimes z\longmapsto\rho_m(r)z,$$
with inverses $z\mapsto1\otimes z$, are isomorphisms of complexes of $(A_{L,m})_Y$-modules, commute with every reduction transition, and compute $R_E[0]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{L,m}$. For $L=E$ they identify the canonical derived reduction units $c_m:R_E[0]\to\operatorname{Res}_m(R_E[0]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m})$ of the reduction tower [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], computed with $q=\mathrm{id}_P$ and the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], with the projections $\pi^E_m$, i.e. $u_m\circ\gamma_m=\pi^E_m$ for $\gamma_m(r)=r\otimes1$. There exists exactly one $R_L$-linear chain map $\eta_{E,L}:R_L[0]\to C_{E,L}$ such that, for every site object $V$, every $s\in R_L(V)$, and every $m\ge1$, the $m$-th coordinate of $\mathrm{fst}\circ\eta_{E,L}$ in degree zero sends $s$ to $1\otimes\pi^L_m(s)$, and every component of $\mathrm{snd}\circ\eta_{E,L}$ is zero. Equivalently the degree-zero coordinate condition may be imposed only on the unit section $1\in R_L(V)$ for every $V$. No quasi-isomorphism or constructibility assertion is included here.

proof.text: For any sheaf $M$ of $R_E$-modules, sectionwise multiplication $M(V)\otimes_{R_E(V)}R_E(V)\to M(V)$ has inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$: the balancing relation gives $x\otimes r=rx\otimes1$. These inverses commute with restriction. Thus the presheaf tensor is already isomorphic to the sheaf $M$, and sheafification gives $M\otimes_{R_E}R_E\cong M$, naturally in $M$. Tensoring with $R_E$ is consequently the identity functor and is exact, so $R_E$ is flat by the definition of flatness. Tensoring with the zero sheaf is zero (every elementary tensor has zero second factor), hence zero is flat as well. For any acyclic complex $F$, the degree-$n$ direct-sum total tensor with $P=R_E[0]$ has just the summand $F^n\otimes_{R_E}R_E\cong F^n$; its differential is $d_F^n$ because $d_P=0$. It is therefore isomorphic to $F$ as a complex, hence acyclic. This proves K-flatness directly from its definition and proves that every term of $P$ is flat.

proof.text: Write $S_m=(A_{L,m})_Y$. The balanced map $R_E(V)\otimes_{R_E(V)}S_m(V)\to S_m(V)$ sends $r\otimes z$ to $\rho_m(r)z$. Its inverse sends $z$ to $1\otimes z$: their composites are the identity since $1\otimes\rho_m(r)z=r\otimes z$ and $\rho_m(1)z=z$. Both maps are $S_m(V)$-linear and commute with restrictions. Thus they are inverse presheaf morphisms and induce inverse morphisms after sheafification, giving $u_m$ and its stated inverse. All complexes in this calculation are concentrated in degree zero, so these maps commute with differentials. Step 1 permits the identity K-flat resolution of $P$. The definition of scalar extension along $\rho_m$ then says exactly that this termwise tensor computes $R_E[0]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{L,m}$; the base ring for the tensor is the completed sheaf $R_E$, as stipulated in that definition.

source.place: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product; unit calculation; scalar extension uses Bhatt-Scholze Definition 3.5.2 notation

proof.text:
Let $a_m:S_{m+1}\to S_m$ be reduction. The coefficient maps obey $a_m\rho_{m+1}=\rho_m$ and $a_m\pi^L_{m+1}=\pi^L_m$. On elementary tensors,
$$a_m\bigl(u_{m+1}(r\otimes z)\bigr)=a_m(\rho_{m+1}(r)z)=\rho_m(r)a_m(z)=u_m(r\otimes a_m(z)).$$
Equality on elementary tensors gives equality of the presheaf maps, hence equality of the sheafified maps; this proves transition compatibility of $u_m$, and therefore of their inverses. When $L=E$, the derived-reduction definition uses the same tensor along $\pi^E_m$. In the reduction-tower formula $c_m=[\gamma_m]\circ[q]^{-1}$ choose $q=\mathrm{id}_P$. Then $u_m\gamma_m(r)=u_m(r\otimes1)=\pi^E_m(r)$, as sheaf morphisms and hence also after localization to the derived category.

source.place: Coefficient-object paragraph; direct reduction calculation with the models of the cited definitions

proof.text:
For every $m$ define $h_m:R_L\to T_m^0$ by $h_m(s)=1\otimes\pi^L_m(s)$, using the inverse $u_m^{-1}$ of Step 2. This is a sheaf morphism: it commutes with restriction, is additive, and for $b,s\in R_L(V)$ satisfies
$$h_m(bs)=1\otimes\pi^L_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)=b\cdot(1\otimes\pi^L_m(s))=b\cdot h_m(s),$$
where the target action is restriction along $\pi^L_m$. Thus it is $R_L$-linear. From Step 3, $t_mh_{m+1}(s)=1\otimes a_m\pi^L_{m+1}(s)=h_m(s)$. The tuple $h(s)=(h_m(s))_m$ defines a sheaf map to $B^0$: tuples restrict coordinatewise and glue uniquely coordinatewise because each factor is a sheaf. Its coordinates show $(1-s)h=0$. This uses no exactness or surjectivity of products.

source.place: Coefficient-object paragraph; explicit compatible quotient-coordinate map to the scalar tower

proof.text: Put $D=1-s$. Every $T_m$ and hence $B$ is concentrated in degree zero. Unpack the strict mapping cocone $C=\operatorname{Cone}(D)[-1]$: in its normalized $(\mathrm{fst},\mathrm{snd})$ coordinates, $C^n=B^n\oplus B^{n-1}$ and its differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Bx,Dx-d_By)$. Here the usual cone differential and the minus sign of the shift give this formula after the sign in the strict first projection is included. In particular $C^0=B^0\oplus0$, $C^1=0\oplus B^0$, all other terms vanish, and $d_C^0(x,0)=(0,Dx)$. Define $\eta^0(s)=(h(s),0)$ in these coordinates and $\eta^n=0$ for $n\ne0$. Step 4 gives $d_C^0\eta^0(s)=(0,Dh(s))=0$. Every other chain-map equation has a zero source term or zero source differential, so also holds. This is the required $R_L$-linear chain map in the strict complex, with the stated first coordinates and zero second component, before localization.

source.place: Coefficient-object paragraph; strict cone normalization, using the cone and signed-shift formulas in the cited definition

proof.text:
Suppose $\eta'$ is another map satisfying the coordinates. In degree zero the product coordinates of $\mathrm{fst}\eta'$ equal all $h_m$, so $\mathrm{fst}\eta'=h$ there. Its second coordinate is zero by hypothesis. A map into the graded direct sum underlying the cone is determined by these two coordinates, hence $\eta'^0=\eta^0$. All source terms in other degrees are zero, so their components are the unique zero maps. This proves equality of the chain maps. Finally suppose only the unit-section condition is imposed. For every object $V$ and every $b\in R_L(V)$, $R_L(V)$-linearity gives
$$(\mathrm{fst}\eta')_m(b)=b\cdot(\mathrm{fst}\eta')_m(1)=b\cdot(1\otimes1)=1\otimes\pi^L_m(b).$$
Thus the unit condition implies the full condition, and the converse is its specialization at $b=1$. This also covers the zero ring of sections, where $1=0$.
